title: Setting Off
subtitle: A trip from the airport to New York to Washington, told almost entirely in phrasal verbs.
description: A B2 travel reading and listening text built on the phrasal verbs of journeys — set off, check in, touch down, head over, look back on — with vocabulary and comprehension exercises.
passage: Anna and Mark had been planning their trip to the United States for months, and the day had finally come to set off. They had packed up their suitcases the night before and made sure to check in online for the flight, so that the morning would be one thing less to worry about.

At the airport they checked in their luggage and went through security without any trouble. That left a couple of hours before boarding, so they browsed around the duty-free shops. Anna found a perfume she liked and picked it up as a souvenir.

Once they had boarded, they settled in for the long flight. Mark pulled out his tablet to watch a film; Anna dozed off almost before the plane had levelled out. The flight was smooth, and they touched down in New York in the early afternoon.

After they got through customs they picked up their rental car and headed out to the hotel. They were keen to check out Times Square, so once they had freshened up they headed over to it on foot. The lights and the noise were overwhelming in the best way, and they stood there a while taking in the sights and sounds of the city.

The next day they drove down to Washington, D.C. They set out early to get ahead of the traffic and made good time on the road. When they arrived they checked into their new hotel and set off again to explore the National Mall, walking around the monuments and taking in the history behind each one.

Over the rest of the trip they ate out at one local restaurant after another, picked up a few more souvenirs, and met up with an old friend who had moved to the States some years earlier. When the time came to pack up and head back home they were sorry to go, but they had a great many photographs to look back on.

On the last morning they checked out of the hotel, dropped off the rental car and headed to the airport. As they boarded the flight home, they found themselves already looking forward to the next trip.

exercises.title: Understanding the Text
exercises.instructions: Some of these ask you to work out what happened from the way it is described.

items.prompt: Why did Anna and Mark check in online the night before?
options: Because the airline charges for checking in at the airport
To leave themselves one less thing to deal with on the morning of the flight
Because their luggage was too heavy for the desk
items.explanation: “So that the morning would be one thing less to worry about.”

items.prompt: “Anna dozed off almost before the plane had levelled out.” What does this tell us?
options: That she fell asleep very soon after take-off
That she was unwell during the climb
That the flight was delayed on the runway
items.explanation: A plane levels out a few minutes after take-off; she was asleep before then.

items.prompt: “Check in” and “check out” both appear twice in this text, with different meanings each time. Which pair is correct?
options: Check in = board a plane / arrive at a hotel; check out = pay a bill / buy something
Check in = hand over luggage / register at a hotel; check out = go and see something / leave a hotel after paying
Check in = look at something / register; check out = depart / land
items.explanation: They check in their luggage and check into the Washington hotel; they check out Times Square (go and see it) and check out of the hotel on the last morning.

items.prompt: Why did they set out early for Washington?
options: To arrive before the monuments closed
To get ahead of the traffic
Because the rental car had to be returned that day
items.explanation: “They set out early to get ahead of the traffic and made good time on the road.”

items.prompt: What does “made good time” mean here?
options: They arrived at exactly the planned hour
The drive took less time than expected
items.explanation: To make good time is to travel faster than you had allowed for — the result of leaving before the traffic.

items.prompt: The text says the lights and noise of Times Square were “overwhelming in the best way”. What is being conveyed?
options: That the experience was intense and they enjoyed it
That they found the crowds unpleasant
That they could not see properly
items.explanation: “Overwhelming” is usually negative; “in the best way” turns it round — too much, and welcome for it.

items.prompt: How does the text end, in terms of the travellers' feelings?
options: Relieved to be going home after a tiring trip
Sorry to leave, but already anticipating the next journey
Undecided about whether they would travel again
items.explanation: “They were sorry to go”, and by the final line they are “already looking forward to the next trip”.

exercises.title: Choose the Particle
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with the particle that gives the meaning the situation needs.

items.prompt: We set ___ at six in the morning to avoid the worst of the traffic.
items.explanation: To set out is to begin a journey, usually with the time mentioned. Set off would also work; set in and set over would not.

items.prompt: The plane touched ___ twenty minutes ahead of schedule.
items.explanation: An aircraft touches down when it lands.

items.prompt: I dozed ___ during the film and missed the ending.
items.explanation: To doze off is to fall lightly asleep without meaning to.

items.prompt: We're meeting ___ ___ some friends at the restaurant at eight.
items.explanation: To meet up with someone is to meet them by arrangement.

items.prompt: Can you drop the car ___ at the rental desk before we go to the gate?
items.explanation: To drop something off is to take it somewhere and leave it.
Look forward to is about the future; look back on is about the past.

items.prompt: It's a trip we'll look ___ ___ for years.
items.explanation: To look back on something is to remember and reflect on it.

exercises.title: The Verbs of a Journey
exercises.instructions: Match each phrasal verb to what it means in this text.

pairs.right: to make yourself comfortable in a new place
to wash and tidy yourself after travelling
to look at things without intending to buy
to look at something and absorb it
to complete a process such as customs
to have a meal in a restaurant
to return to where you came from

items.explanation: Several of these share a particle with a different sense elsewhere — compare take in here with take in meaning to deceive, or get through meaning to finish a task.

exercises.title: True or False?
exercises.instructions: Decide whether each statement matches the text.

items.statement: They had problems at airport security.
items.explanation: False — they “went through security without any trouble”.

items.statement: Anna bought the perfume as a gift for someone else.
items.explanation: False — she “picked it up as a souvenir”, which is something kept as a reminder of the trip.

items.statement: They travelled from New York to Washington by car.
items.explanation: True — they drove down, having picked up a rental car in New York.

items.statement: The friend they met had recently moved to the United States.
items.explanation: False — the friend “had moved to the States some years earlier”.

items.statement: They returned the rental car before going to the airport.
items.explanation: True — “they checked out of the hotel, dropped off the rental car and headed to the airport”.

discussion: Describe your last journey using at least eight phrasal verbs from this text.
Which is better on a short trip — planning every day in advance, as Anna and Mark did, or deciding as you go?
“Check out” means two quite different things in this text. Find another English verb that changes meaning with its particle, and explain both senses.
Is a souvenir worth buying? What do you actually keep from a trip?
Write about 150 words describing a journey you would like to make, from setting off to heading back.
